Judicial Branch testimony neither for nor against LD 1842, An Act to
Establish Stepparent Visitation Rights

Senator Carney, Representative Kuhn, members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Judiciary, my name is Barbara Cardone and I represent the Judicial Branch. I would like to
provide the following testimony neither for nor against this bill to address the fiscal implications of this bill.
LD l842 would create a new cause of action in the District Courts for stepparents to
obtain court-ordered visitation with a stepchild. The bill establishes a process similar to grandparent visitation matters, but with some distinctions.
While it is not possible to estimate exactly the volume of cases this bill would create, it
would necessarily increase the number of filings in the District Court as any new cause of action
does. Therefore, the Maine Judicial Branch will be submitting a fiscal note seeking the resources commensurate with what it thinks would be necessary to process these matters.
Thank you for your time. I would be happy to answer any questions.

195660:
Good morning Senator Rotundo, Representative Cloutier, Representative McCabe and members of the
committee.
My name is Brenda Hathaway and I support this bill.
My stepdaughter had two homes for four years. The only gift I ever saw make her cry was a necklace I
gave her that said "Big Sis" and contained the names of her siblings from both households.
At age 11, her father was killed in the Lewiston mass shooting.
Gatekeeping began immediately. We went from 50/50 custody to being at the mercy of her mother's
whims. The gatekeeping applied to the entirety of her father's family as well.
When I did get to talk with my stepdaughter she asked what was going to happen to us. She wanted the
old schedule back. (In court, that would have been hearsay.)
I asked for advice from social workers, lawyers, doctors, other parents, therapists, anyone. Her
grandmother and I were both told I had a better chance at De Facto Parental Rights than she did with
Grandparents' Rights.
I filed for De Facto Parental Rights and a few days later my stepdaughter and her mother disappeared. They ghosted an entire community of people. Multiple people called DHHS, another avenue which
seems to have failed. I did not have standing to be able to request a Guardian ad litem.
My stepdaughter was not allowed to say goodbye to the Hathaway family or even to her own friends. Belongings at my house--gone. Activities-gone. Support system--gone. She lost her father and then she
lost her voice, she lost her rights, she lost her world.
At my hearing, I did not prove that her mother understood, acknowledged, or accepted me as a parent. It was not enough that her father did because "One parent cannot unilaterally `cause an
unconstitutional dilution of another's legal parent's rights"'
I did not try to prove her mother was unfit; that was not in my stepdaughter 's best interests. I did state what her mother's actions had been. It seems to me that since I did not prove her mother was unfit it
was then presumed that her mother's actions had been in her child's best interest.
The law failed. No one should be alienated from their family regardless of biological or legal
comiection.
My stepdaughter loves her mother, but the mental health consequences of this on my stepdaughter will
be severe and long lasting. And to me it feels wholly unnecessary and heartbreaking.
I hope you will consider my story not only for passing this bill but for the wording of the bill if it's
passed.
Thank you for your time and consideration.

Testimony in Support of LD 1842
"An Act to Establish Stepparent Visitation Rights. "
Presented to the Joint Standing Committee on Judiciary
May 16, 2025
Good afternoon Senator Carney, Representative Kuhn, and the distinguished members of the Joint
Standing Committee on Judiciary. My name is Peggy Rotundo, and I have the privilege of representing the City of Lewiston in District 21. I am here today to introduce LD 1842, "An Act to Establish
Stepparent Visitation Rights."
On October 25, 2023, Maxx Hathaway was killed in the mass shooting in Lewiston. He left behind, his pregnant wife, Brenda, their daughter, Lilian, and Maxx's ll year old daughter, Zoey. Maxx and Zoey's biological mother had shared custody of Zoey, who felt very much a part of the loving Hathaway family.
She was very close to father, her stepmother, Brenda, and her half-sister, Lilian.
Immediately after the shooting, Zoey's biological mother removed the cl1ild from the Hathaway home, creating one more tragic loss for Zoey and for the Hathaway family. For more than 6 months, Zoey was
not allowed to speak to anyone, her sister, step mother, grandparents, aunts/uncles, cousins or friends.
Brenda, her step mother, was frantic with worry during this time. She had no idea where her step daughter was or how she was. She had no idea if she was getting the emotional support she needed after the trauma
she had experienced. She could only hope and pray that she was OK and hoped that Zoey knew that the
Hathaway family loved her and was trying desperately to establish contact with her. Brenda filed for De
Facto Parental rights, but found she had no standing as a step parent. All of this re-traumatized a family that had experienced one of the most horrific experiences imaginable. Zoey's mother continues to tightly control the small number of people Zoey can speak with and even this communication is erratic.
I started to work with Brenda and her attorney after I heard Brenda's heartbreaking story. The proposed bill you have before you is an attempt to address the problem Brenda faced as she worked to establish contact with Zoey. The bill establishes stepparent visitation rights, which don't now exist in Maine statute. It would give stepparents like Brenda standing for contact.
